A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OP3DSG and UniGraph3D work, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 ends with references; v2 retains the main paper and adds Supplementary Sections A-C. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original node, edge, and affordance evaluations, localization sensitivity tests, component ablations, and robot demonstrations in Sections 5-6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds efficiency measurements, ReplicaSSG evaluation, source-dataset breakdowns, and qualitative failure cases in Supplementary Section A.

M1.justification: The detection, part-aware fusion, prior-graph construction, and LLM reasoning procedures in Section 4 are unchanged. Supplementary Section B supplies implementation details, including SAM and robot execution components, without establishing a change to the underlying procedures.

E1.justification: v1 lists ReplicaSSG only in the dataset comparison table. v2 actually evaluates object-centric graph generation on its 11 indoor scenes and nine spatial relation types (Section A.2, Table 7), substantially extending validation beyond UniGraph3D. The source-dataset breakdowns reuse data already represented in UniGraph3D.

E2.justification: The retained UniGraph3D comparisons contain the same ConceptGraph, FunGraph, OpenFunGraph, and KeySG variants. The added supplementary comparisons use subsets of existing ConceptGraph/OpenFunGraph variants; no new comparison method or replacement in a corresponding retained experiment is established.

E3.justification: Section A.1 adds an efficiency evaluation using detection-stage peak GPU memory and graph-construction VLM/LLM call counts. Existing retrieval, localization, and ablation protocols remain unchanged, and Section A.3 explicitly preserves detector and LLM settings for the source-dataset evaluations.

E4.justification: The original ablations and localization sensitivity study remain unchanged. v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence through efficiency analysis, source-dataset breakdowns examining dependence on benchmark merging, and multi-scene case studies documenting occlusion, reflection, and thin-object recognition failures (Sections A.1, A.3-A.4).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates; the dataset-frequency plots do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1-5 retain their numerical values, while Tables 6-9 add substantial results. Table 6 reports detection-stage peak memory of 8.08 GB for OP3DSG, 11.43 GB for ConceptGraph, and 11.90 GB for OpenFunGraph; Table 7 adds ReplicaSSG scores, including OP3DSG object R@3 of 59.7. Source-dataset scores, qualitative failures, and label-frequency plots are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The graph formulation in Section 3 and mathematical definitions and equations in Section 4 are unchanged. The supplement adds experimental analysis and documentation without introducing new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified scene graphs, OP3DSG, UniGraph3D, performance, and robotic applicability. The supplement adds supporting evidence without redefining those core contributions.

C2.justification: The supplement substantially extends interpretation through arguments about generalization beyond the unified benchmark, dependence on dataset merging, and specific occlusion/reflection/misclassification failure mechanisms. It also qualifies memory measurements as detection-stage only. Section A.3 overstates uniform superiority: Table 9 gives SceneFun3D spatial R@3 of 61.5 for OP3DSG versus 62.1 for OpenFunGraph++.

D1.justification: Sections B-C supply substantial information absent from v1: SAM mask extraction, saturation/value thresholds of 0.1/0.9, histogram weights of 0.2/0.4/0.4, part-fusion weight 0.4, HomeRobot execution, and A* navigation. They also document the 11 canonical relation labels and nine affordance categories. These are disclosures about existing work, rather than demonstrated setting changes.

R1.justification: v2 retains all 64 original references and adds four works supporting supplementary details: A*, Segment Anything, LLaVA, and HomeRobot. The related-work discussion and central positioning remain unchanged; other citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain essentially unchanged. v2 appends an organized supplement with a contents list and Sections A-C, alongside a small corresponding-author footnote edit; there is no extensive rewriting of the existing paper.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6-10, a six-panel scene visualization in Figure 6, and two label-frequency charts in Figure 7. These substantially expand the presentation of evidence and dataset documentation. Existing main-paper figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 fills important gaps in v1, which referred readers to supplementary implementation and dataset details that were absent from the supplied PDF. Explicit fusion settings and annotation categories improve reproducibility, while ReplicaSSG evaluation, source-dataset breakdowns, and failure cases substantially strengthen empirical assessment. The detection-only memory scope and overbroad superiority statement in Section A.3 temper, but do not outweigh, these gains.
